newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium futures down, tracking LME, dollar.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium futures down, tracking LME, dollar.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures closed lower on Wednesday, tracking the metal's decline on the London Metal Exchange (LME) overnight and the dollar's fall, traders said.
"We saw quite a lot of stop-loss selling by individual investors, though the dollar's slight recovery in the afternoon triggered some bargain hunting," said one trader.
"People feel it's difficult to buy as the market abroad looks weak and many are worried about the dollar's fall."
The June and April contract both shed 2.8 yen to end at 184.3 and 185.6 yen respectively. Others were down between 3.5 yen and 4.7 yen.
Estimated volume was a relatively heavy 5,310 lots.

In London overnight, aluminium was last quoted at $1,555/$1,557 per tonne, dragged down by a sharp decline of copper triggered by a slump on COMEX. Three-month aluminium lost $22 by the kerb close to $1,565.
